moat_against: Regulators cap the return — OCC, Arkansas PSC and FERC set allowed ROE and recovery; roic_proxy was only 5.05%-6.31% in FY2020-FY2025, never well above the cost of capital

No pricing power and fuel pass-through volatility — gross margin swung from 40.71% (FY2021, Winter Storm Uri) to 65.03% (FY2023) to 60.52% (FY2025); earnings are weather- and rate-case-timing-driven (Q1 2026 EPS $0.24 vs $0.31 a year earlier on milder weather)

Growth capex consumes the cash — capex $1,178.2M / $1,090.9M / $1,054.4M in FY2023-FY2025 against D&A of $506.6M / $539.5M / $559.8M, so conservative owner's earnings were positive in only 2 of the last 5 years

Leverage and dilution fund the plan — net debt $5,661M at FY2025 and equity issuance to fund capex (diluted shares 207,200,000 in Q1 2026 vs 201,900,000 in Q1 2025); single-state Oklahoma concentration and coal/gas transition and large-load contract risk (Google / large-load tariff still being finalized)
moat_for: Exclusive regulated electric franchise — OG&E serves ~913,305 customers in Oklahoma and western Arkansas with captive, essential-service demand
Visible rate-base compounding — $7.3B capital plan 2026-2030, management guides 5-7% EPS growth through 2030 off the 2026 midpoint of $2.43/share, targeting the top half in 2027-2028

Real load growth — weather-normalized load +6.6% in 2025, 4-6% expected in 2026, retail load up >24% since 2021; large-load / data-center demand (Google facilities) and SPP transmission assignments add duration
Stable regulated returns — ROE ~9.2-9.5% in FY2023-FY2025 and operating income rising $650.2M / $745.3M / $799.4M over the same years; 17 years of dividend growth in fundamentals.json
moat_justification: Regulated electric monopoly: OG&E is the exclusive regulated electric utility for ~913,305 customers (FY2025 10-K) in Oklahoma and western Arkansas, with essential inelastic demand, rate-base recovery and a $7.3B 2026-2030 capital plan guided to 5-7% EPS growth through 2030 — a durable, visible franchise. Capped at 5 (moderate/narrow) because the return evidence does not support a wide moat: fundamentals.json roic_proxy stayed in a narrow 5.05%-6.31% band in FY2020-FY2025 (5.71% / 5.05% / 6.17% / 6.13% / 6.22% / 6.31%) and ROE was ~9.2-9.5% in FY2023-FY2025 — regulator-set returns at/below the cost of capital, not pricing power above it. Gross margin (fuel is largely pass-through) was 60.52% in FY2025 after 63.09% in FY2024 and 65.03% in FY2023, volatile in the Uri/midstream years (40.71% in FY2021). No pricing power beyond Oklahoma Corporation Commission / Arkansas PSC / FERC rate cases, single-state concentration, and growth funded with debt plus equity (forward equity for ~4.6M shares; Q1 2026 diluted count 207,200,000 vs 201,900,000 a year earlier). A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years.
name: OGE ENERGY CORP.
one_liner: Durable regulated Oklahoma utility, moat 5/10, but on a TTM owner's-earnings base of $1.01/share the weighted IRR is only 5.29% (IV@15% $9.98 vs $46.81) — Tier D, sector-model misfit at low confidence; it clears 15% only below ~$9.98, because growth capex runs at ~2x D&A and regulators cap the return.
